pages.text: "Mom, wait! I have not finished counting." Riri in her yellow hat counted on her fingers at a button stall. One, two, three... Mom in her blue apron had already walked far ahead.
Today, Riri wanted to choose the shiniest shell button. "This one is pretty, and that one too..." She started counting from the beginning again. The blue apron disappeared between the stalls.
She looked up, but could not see the blue apron. Strangers' legs passed back and forth. Riri's heart thumped, and tears filled her eyes.

On the verge of tears, Riri remembered Mom's words. "If you get lost, stop right where you are!" Instead of running, Riri planted both feet together. Phew, one deep breath. "It is all right. I am here."
Staying there, Riri lifted her chin and called loudly. "Mom—!" Once, twice, three times. Her voice carried between the stalls. Her feet did not move one step.
Splashing footsteps approached over the wet ground. Lolo in yellow boots ran through the stalls to Riri. "Here! Riri is here!" Lolo waved both hands and shouted.
The blue apron appeared among the people. Riri nestled into Mom's arms. Mom put the apron's edge firmly in Riri's hand. "Hold the blue apron tight!"
All three returned to the button stall. Riri kept hold of the apron. With one hand on it, she chose one button with the other. "This one!" The shiniest shell button.
On every market day, Riri remembered three things. One, hold the apron tight! Two, if you lose it, stop there! Three, call Mom loudly! Beside her, Lolo repeated, "Hold the blue apron tight!"
That evening, Riri sat on Mom's lap, still gripping the apron. Even if lost, she could stop and call, and Mom would find her. "Mom, next market day I will hold tight too. Hold the blue apron tight!"
